skill.name: hugging-face-jobs
skill.description: Run Python, Docker, GPU, TPU, and scheduled workloads on Hugging Face Jobs. The skill guides authentication, secrets, hardware selection, timeouts, monitoring, and result persistence.
skill.summary: Submit and manage Hugging Face Jobs for cloud compute, batch inference, data processing, and ML experiments.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, documentation URLs, and example code blocks. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found. The main residual risk is that the skill can launch paid remote jobs and handle HF_TOKEN secrets, so explicit confirmation is needed before submission.

remediation.issue: Paid remote job submission can happen without a required approval checkpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Add an instruction to estimate cost and get explicit user confirmation before launching or scheduling any Hugging Face job.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded and environment-variable token examples may be copied into real jobs.
remediation.suggestion: Remove literal token examples and show only secret-based placeholders. Avoid printing token prefixes in troubleshooting examples.

remediation.issue: External result upload examples can move user data outside Hugging Face.
remediation.suggestion: Require the user to choose the destination and confirm data handling before S3, GCS, or API uploads.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Paid Job Submission Needs Explicit Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs assistants to always submit workloads with hf_jobs and notes that Jobs require a paid plan. Launching jobs without a confirmation step can spend user resources and run code remotely.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The directive to use hf_jobs is explicit, and the prerequisite section states that Jobs require paid access. The risk is operational misuse, not hidden malware.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Token Handling Examples Appear in Documentation
semantic_findings.description: The skill shows hardcoded and environment-variable token examples, even while labeling them less secure. Users may copy these patterns into jobs or logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The insecure examples are clearly present but also marked as not recommended. This lowers severity while still making the documentation risk real.

semantic_findings.title: External Result Uploads Need User-Selected Destinations
semantic_findings.description: The skill lists S3 and API uploads as persistence options without requiring data classification or destination confirmation. This could expose user data if reused carelessly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples are legitimate persistence options, but they involve moving results to external services. The finding is contextual and depends on user data sensitivity.

content.user_title: Run Workloads on Hugging Face Jobs
content.value_statement: Cloud ML jobs can be hard to size, authenticate, monitor, and save correctly. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a practical workflow for Hugging Face Jobs.
actual_capabilities: Plan UV script and Docker jobs for Hugging Face Jobs infrastructure.
Recommend CPU, GPU, or TPU hardware for common workload sizes.
Guide secure HF_TOKEN use through job secrets for Hub operations.
Set timeouts, monitoring steps, and cancellation paths for submitted jobs.
Plan result persistence to the Hub, object storage, or user APIs.
Create scheduled jobs and webhook-triggered job workflows.
limitations: Requires a Hugging Face account with Jobs access.
Job execution can consume paid compute resources.
Does not validate every user script for correctness or safety.
Private Hub operations require a correctly scoped HF_TOKEN.

use_cases.title: Process Large Datasets
use_cases.description: Data teams can transform large datasets on managed workers and push clean outputs to the Hugging Face Hub.

use_cases.title: Run Batch Inference
use_cases.description: ML teams can choose GPU hardware, run model inference at scale, and save generated responses for review.

use_cases.title: Automate Recurring Jobs
use_cases.description: Operations teams can schedule reports, dataset refreshes, or repository-triggered jobs with clear monitoring steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Test Job
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small workload
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a quick Hugging Face Jobs test for my Python workload. Recommend hardware, timeout, persistence, and approval checks before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Batch Inference
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a batch inference job for [dataset] using [model]. Start with a small validation run, then describe the scale-up plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design Scheduled Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a scheduled Hugging Face job that refreshes [dataset] every [schedule] and saves results to [repo]. Include monitoring and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a GPU Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a cost-aware GPU job plan for [workload]. Compare hardware options, token requirements, timeout, persistence, and recovery steps before submission.

output_examples.input: Run sentiment analysis on 50,000 product reviews and save the results.
output: A small validation job is recommended before the full run.
The plan selects appropriate hardware, timeout, Hub persistence, and monitoring details.

output_examples.input: Schedule a weekly dataset quality report on Hugging Face Jobs.
output: The output is a scheduled job plan with timing, token needs, and result storage.
It includes inspection, log review, cancellation, and failure recovery steps.

output_examples.input: Choose hardware for a large batch inference workload.
output: The response compares GPU choices, estimated runtime, timeout buffer, and cost controls.
It recommends starting small before scaling to larger hardware.

best_practices: Start with the smallest useful hardware and a short validation run.
Pass tokens through secrets and use the least required permission scope.
Choose a persistence target before launch and share monitoring details after submission.
anti_patterns: Launching paid GPU jobs without explicit user confirmation.
Hardcoding tokens in scripts, environment variables, or logs.
Running long jobs without a timeout and result persistence plan.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan, submit, monitor, schedule, and persist workloads on Hugging Face Jobs.

faq.question: Does it require Hugging Face Jobs access?
faq.answer: Yes. Users need an account and plan that can run Hugging Face Jobs.

faq.question: Can it use GPUs or TPUs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for CPU, GPU, and TPU hardware selection.

faq.question: How are tokens handled?
faq.answer: The skill recommends passing HF_TOKEN through job secrets instead of hardcoding credentials.

faq.question: Does it save results automatically?
faq.answer: No. It helps choose a persistence method because job files are temporary.

faq.question: Can it schedule recurring jobs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers scheduled jobs, webhooks, inspection, suspension, resume, and deletion workflows.
